anthropic_claude_news.title: Anthropic's Opus 5 blows past Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol on the benchmark designed to measure real intelligence
anthropic_claude_news.summary: Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 scored 30.2% on ARC-AGI-3, nearly quadrupling GPT-5.6 Sol's prior record of 7.8% on a benchmark built to measure fluid, human-like reasoning. Its developers say Opus 5 formulated strategies independently rather than pattern-matching training data. It cements Anthropic's frontier-reasoning lead heading into the Claude 5 generation. Automation angle: Re-run your Claude Code portfolio demos on Opus 5 this week and post the before/after — living proof you build on the current frontier model.

ai_business_automation.title: AI adoption reshapes workflows and hiring across high-growth technology companies: Report
ai_business_automation.summary: A new report finds high-growth tech firms are embedding AI across engineering, finance, and HR, reshaping both workflows and hiring plans. Most respondents expect AI to change headcount within a year, marking a shift from pilots to org-wide deployment. Automation angle: Package a 'department AI audit → 3 automations' offer — exactly the entry point the companies in this report are buying.

ai_business_automation.title: Monday.com is the latest tech company to blame AI for layoffs — here are 20 others
ai_business_automation.summary: Monday.com joins a growing list — TechCrunch counts 20+ tech companies this year — citing AI as a stated factor in layoffs. It marks AI moving from a productivity add-on to a headcount lever across the sector. Automation angle: Position your automations as capacity multipliers for lean teams — today's buyers are companies trying to do more with fewer people.

quantum_ai_research.title: 76 Quantum Theorems Completed By AI In New Lean 4 Benchmarks - Quantum Zeitgeist
quantum_ai_research.summary: An AI system completed 76 quantum-information theorems in new Lean 4 formal-proof benchmarks, showing agent models can produce machine-checkable proofs in quantum math. It's early evidence AI can accelerate quantum-algorithm research, not just classical coding. Automation angle: Formal-proof agents are a rising niche — a small Lean + LLM demo is a differentiated portfolio piece.

quantum_ai_research.title: Argonne AI Cuts Quantum Circuit Design Time For Nuclear Physics - Quantum Zeitgeist
quantum_ai_research.summary: Argonne researchers used AI to slash the time needed to design quantum circuits for nuclear-physics simulations. It's a clean example of machine learning compressing an expensive quantum-engineering step. Automation angle: 'AI-assisted design' workflows generalize — frame client automations the same way, as time-compression on expert tasks.

quantum_ai_research.title: BlueQubit Secures $1.5M DOE Grants For AI-Driven Quantum Error Correction - Quantum Zeitgeist
quantum_ai_research.summary: BlueQubit won $1.5M in DOE grants to build AI-driven quantum error correction, using ML decoders to tame qubit noise. Error correction is the gating problem for useful quantum, and AI decoders are a leading bet. Automation angle: Follow ML-for-QEC as a hiring signal — labs funding it need ML engineers, not only physicists.

quantum_ai_research.title: Rice Builds AI To Tackle Quantum Optimization Bottlenecks - Quantum Zeitgeist
quantum_ai_research.summary: Rice University built AI methods to break through bottlenecks in quantum optimization problems, targeting where near-term quantum hardware stalls. Optimization is among the most shippable quantum use cases. Automation angle: Optimization framing sells — watch this space for real client problems you could tackle with classical ML today.

quantum_ai_research.title: Quantum X Labs Validates AI Decoder On Surface-Code Simulations - Quantum Zeitgeist
quantum_ai_research.summary: Quantum X Labs validated an AI decoder on surface-code simulations, a key step toward real-time quantum error correction. Neural decoders can keep pace with fast error streams better than classical ones. Automation angle: Neural decoders show how latency-critical inference gets deployed — a transferable systems-engineering lesson.

quantum_ai_research.title: WISER and E.ON Advance Energy Demand Forecasting with Quantum Machine Learning
quantum_ai_research.summary: WISER and E.ON applied quantum machine learning to energy-demand forecasting, testing whether QML improves on classical models for grid load — a rare real-industry QML pilot. Automation angle: Energy/grid forecasting is a lucrative ML niche even without quantum, and a strong portfolio domain.

quantum_ai_research.title: IonQ, QuantumBasel Study Suggests Hybrid AI Workloads Could Gain Energy Advantages From Quantum Hardware as Systems Scale - The Quantum Insider
quantum_ai_research.summary: An IonQ / QuantumBasel study suggests hybrid AI workloads could gain energy advantages from quantum hardware as systems scale, pitching quantum co-processors for specific AI sub-tasks. The claim is early and scale-dependent. Automation angle: Track hybrid quantum-AI architecture claims skeptically — energy-per-inference is the metric that matters.

quantum_ai_research.title: New Framework Uses Quantum Geometry to Help Quantum AI Systems Remember What They Learn - The Quantum Insider
quantum_ai_research.summary: A new framework uses quantum geometry to help quantum AI systems retain what they learn, tackling catastrophic forgetting in quantum models and bridging continual learning with quantum computation. Automation angle: Continual-learning problems recur in classical AI too — a fundable, research-adjacent theme to demo.

elon_musk_ai_vision.summary: xAI is pushing Grok Imagine, its image/video generation feature, as a headline consumer capability for Grok, with coverage breaking down its four core pillars. It marks xAI's move from chat into generative media, positioned against OpenAI and Google's models. Automation angle: Watch for Grok Imagine API access — if it opens, a fast 'Grok vs Sora' comparison reel is easy content and interview small-talk.

elon_musk_ai_vision.title: Grok AI Review 2026: Features, Pricing & Honest Verdict - Memeburn
elon_musk_ai_vision.summary: A 2026 review lays out Grok's current features, pricing tiers, and where it lands versus ChatGPT and Claude: strong real-time X integration, still behind on coding and reasoning. It's useful context for Elon's 'maximally truth-seeking AI' positioning. Automation angle: Know Grok's price/feature envelope so you can recommend the right model per client task instead of defaulting to one.

unaddressed_ai_problems.title: Meta Is Letting Fake AI-Generated Doctors Sell Quack Cures on Its Platforms
unaddressed_ai_problems.summary: Meta is allowing AI-generated 'doctors' to hawk unproven cures across its platforms, targeting people with health conditions. Platform-scale detection of AI-impersonated professionals is unsolved, and moderation lags generation — the victims are the most vulnerable users. Automation angle: Build a demo that flags AI-generated medical/authority impersonation in ad creative — a concrete one-week Claude Code portfolio piece.

unaddressed_ai_problems.title: Hundreds asked ChatGPT for poison and bioweapon recipes and some got step-by-step high school level guides
unaddressed_ai_problems.summary: The WSJ reports hundreds of users elicited step-by-step poison and bioweapon guidance from ChatGPT, and OpenAI downgraded GPT-5's risk rating despite internal high-risk flags. Reliable adversarial safety evals for dangerous-capability elicitation are still an open problem, and red-teaming lags model releases. Automation angle: A reusable red-team harness that scores a model's refusal robustness is both a portfolio standout and a real gap labs are hiring for.

unaddressed_ai_problems.title: Meta Desperately Trying to Ban Creeps Misusing Its AI “Pervert Glasses”
unaddressed_ai_problems.summary: Meta is scrambling to ban misuse of its AI smart glasses for covert recording after the fact, showing safety bolted on post-launch. Real-time consent and privacy controls for always-on wearable AI don't exist yet, and the gap widens as the hardware ships. Automation angle: Prototype an on-device 'recording-intent' detector or consent-signal system — a timely privacy-tech demo.

ai_business_opportunities.title: Cheaper, open and intelligent: Chinese AI models gain ground, as they make inroads in the US
ai_business_opportunities.summary: Cheaper, capable open-weight Chinese models are being adopted by US users and businesses to cut inference costs. That opens a clear arbitrage: build vertical AI apps on cheap open models for SMBs priced out of frontier APIs. Automation angle: Start a 'cost-optimized AI' service that migrates clients from expensive frontier APIs to tuned open models and bill a share of the savings.

ai_business_opportunities.title: The AI coding tutor paradox grows as educators scramble to rethink how they test real skills
ai_business_opportunities.summary: An ACM survey finds 68% of CS educators across 49 countries have already changed exams because students lean on AI — but authentic-skill assessment remains unsolved. That's an open edtech market: project-based eval, proctoring, and AI-use-aware grading, and hiring teams face the same verification gap. Automation angle: Build an AI-era skills-assessment tool (verifiable project rubrics + interview-style checks) for bootcamps and hiring teams — a fresh, underserved niche.

global_ai_news.title: Hugging Face CEO calls for ‘radical transparency’ after ‘unprecedented’ OpenAI hack
global_ai_news.summary: Hugging Face CEO Clement Delangue called for 'radical transparency' after what's described as the first autonomous-agent cyberattack hit OpenAI. He argues an unprecedented incident demands an unprecedented, open response, reframing agent security as an industry-wide concern. Automation angle: Agent security is becoming a buyer category — worth a portfolio demo if you build with agent frameworks.

global_ai_news.title: Eminent Domain Could Be Used to Seize Your Land for AI Data Centers
global_ai_news.summary: Reporting suggests eminent domain could be used to seize private land for AI data-center buildout as compute demand collides with local property rights. It signals how far governments may go to secure AI infrastructure, and litigation looks likely. Automation angle: Macro signal — deep-read only if data-center policy touches a provider you depend on.

global_ai_news.title: US reportedly favors selective bans over blanket restrictions on Chinese open weight models citing security concerns
global_ai_news.summary: The Trump administration reportedly favours targeted bans on specific Chinese AI models over a blanket ban, citing security; OpenAI and Google DeepMind signed an open letter opposing broad restrictions. Model provenance and open-weight policy are now geopolitical questions. Automation angle: Track which open models stay compliant in your region before standardizing a build on them.

ai_self_improvement_rsi.title: AREX: Towards a Recursively Self-Improving Agent for Deep Research
ai_self_improvement_rsi.summary: AREX is a recursively self-improving agent for deep research: it decomposes hard multi-constraint questions and verifies candidate answers constraint-by-constraint, using cheap verification to bootstrap harder discovery. It's a concrete self-improvement loop rather than a manifesto. Automation angle: The verify-then-improve pattern is directly reusable — build a research agent that grades its own drafts before returning them.

ai_self_improvement_rsi.title: Building Self-Evolving AI Agents with OpenSpace Using Skills, MCP, Lineage, and Low-Cost Reuse - MarkTechPost
ai_self_improvement_rsi.summary: A walkthrough of building self-evolving agents with OpenSpace, using skills, MCP, provenance lineage, and low-cost reuse so agents accumulate and recombine capabilities over time. It's a practical take on agents that improve without full retraining. Automation angle: Skills + MCP + reuse is exactly the Claude Code stack — a strong template for a 'self-improving agent' portfolio build.

ai_model_benchmarks.title: White Box Evidence Packages for Policy Audit Reports
ai_model_benchmarks.summary: This arXiv paper asks how reviewers can verify whether an LLM-generated audit report is actually supported by evidence, proposing 'white-box evidence packages' that tie each claim to its source. It's a step toward auditable AI oversight beyond raw benchmark scores. Automation angle: Evidence-linked output is a sellable feature — bolt citation-grounding onto any client-facing AI report you build.

new_ai_tools.title: Cursor's agent swarm suggests cheaper models can handle most coding when frontier models plan the work
new_ai_tools.summary: Cursor asked its upgraded agent swarm and its predecessor to rebuild SQLite in Rust from documentation alone, with no source code. The result suggests cheaper models can handle most coding once a frontier model plans and decomposes the work. It's a concrete blueprint for the plan-with-strong, execute-with-cheap pattern. Automation angle: Wire a Claude Code / MCP setup where Opus plans and a cheaper model executes sub-tasks — a cost-cutting pattern worth a 60-second 'Tool Tested' short.

new_ai_tools.title: Ruff v0.16.0
new_ai_tools.summary: Astral shipped Ruff v0.16.0, a major release of its fast Python linter/formatter, on July 23; Simon Willison flagged it after it silently broke his CI jobs. Version pinning matters now that agentic coding tools lean on Ruff for auto-fixes. Automation angle: Add Ruff to a Claude Code pre-commit hook so your portfolio repos stay clean automatically — and pin the version to avoid surprise CI breaks.
